text:
alex: heads up — acme-prod just opened a support ticket: p99 on /v1/generate jumped from ~250ms to ~1.6s at 03:07 UTC. customer says it started after a steady traffic ramp. link: https://support.acme.example/ticket/7892

maya: saw the same in metrics. KV miss rate for tenant acme spiked ~03:05, prefix miss ratio went from 8% -> 63%. p95 up ~300ms, p99 ~1.6s.

jordan: I pulled node logs. lots of these lines during the window:
```
WARN kv: prefix miss for key=tenant:acme:session:0x8f3a, backend_latency=12ms, fallback_lookup=true
INFO runtime: inflight=(120->450) batching_delay=18ms
ERROR cache: eviction_racing detected on shard-7
```

sam: interesting — eviction_racing on shard-7. did we recently change eviction policy?

maya: nope, policy unchanged. but yesterday's rollout bumped global max_prefix_entries from 50k -> 65k for a subset of clusters (opt-in). doesn't affect acme cluster, but the rollout did change shard affinity hashes (shard mapping table v12).

tanya: acme uses lots of short-lived session prefixes from their SDK (session_id in prompt), high cardinality. if shard mapping changed, hot prefixes might have migrated and caused cache cold starts + heavy backend fetches -> thrash.

alex: customer provided a sample request id: r-0a1b2c3d4e. jordan, can you grep that and attach the request flow (kv key, backend latency)?

jordan: grepped. flow shows kv miss then fallback to remote store ~11ms then writeback. sequence repeated for many concurrent requests: backend queue depth spiked. snippet:
```
req=r-0a1b2c3d4e prefix=tenant:acme:session:0x8f3a kv_op=miss fallback_read_ms=11 writeback=true
req=r-0a1b2c3d4f prefix=tenant:acme:session:0x1c9d kv_op=miss fallback_read_ms=13 writeback=true
```

sam: root cause hypothesis: shard remap + influx of ephemeral high-cardinality prefixes -> cache hotset spill across shards -> eviction storms (eviction_racing) -> elevated backend pressure -> p99 regressions.

support-bot: case 7892: customer-impacting latency. severity=P1. Notified oncall.

maya: immediate mitigations we can try (ordering by invasiveness):
1) pin top-10 hot prefixes for tenant acme on their current shard (temp config) to avoid eviction churn.
2) bump per-shard cache headroom (increase max_entries_shard for affected shard) for 30m.
3) enable aggressive prefix backoff: kv.prefix_hot_backoff_ms=100 (reduces duplicate backend reads).
4) if pressure persists, route acme traffic to a warmed pool (drain and spin up nodes with prewarmed cache).

alex: which is the fastest to apply?

tanya: pinning prefixes is fastest. we have admin endpoint to set sticky prefixes per-tenant:
```
POST /admin/kv/pin_prefixes 
body: {"tenant": "acme", "prefixes": ["tenant:acme:session:0x8f3a","tenant:acme:session:0x1c9d"], "ttl_sec": 1800}
```
I can run it now.

alex: do it. also please add a short-term metric to monitor - pinned_hit_rate and backend_qps.

(tanya runs command)
maya: pinned prefixes applied. monitoring shows backend QPS down 42% for acme within two minutes. p99 trending back toward 320ms.

jordan: I pushed a small server-side patch to reduce eviction parallelism on shard-7 (limit concurrent evictors=2). canary deploying to cluster-acme now.

sam: good call. that should reduce eviction_racing. long term we should:
- add prefix fingerprinting to avoid session_id noise in cache keys (normalize session->session:hashN)
- recommend SDK change: sample-based sticky session ids for high-churn apps
- consider adaptive shard hotset replication for tenants above threshold

alex: agree. action items:
- tanya: keep pinned prefixes for 30m and extend if stable (owner: tanya)
- jordan: watch canary, if stable promote in 10m (owner: jordan)
- maya: open postmortem and include metric plots, customer timeline, and rollout correlation (owner: maya)
- sam: draft SDK recommendation for customers with high session cardinality (owner: sam)

tanya: pinned prefixes extended to 2h after stability check. customer updated: "latency improved, thanks".

alex: we'll follow up with billing/CS to ensure no billing break; this was a performance incident only.

support-bot: case 7892 updated: mitigation applied, customer confirmed improvement, severity -> P2.

maya: notes for postmortem: correlate with shard-map rollout v12, list tenants that hit >50% prefix miss, propose a rollout rollback guard (monitor prefix_miss_ratio per-tenant) before remapping.

jordan: also adding a small repro: loadgen script to reproduce hot ephemeral prefixes:
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello","session_id":"sess-'$RANDOM'"}' &
done
```
This reproduces the pattern in ~2-3 minutes on our dev cluster.

sam: thanks. i'll start draft SDK notes and coordinate with maya for the PM/customer comms.

alex: great work. keep this thread updated if anything regresses.

(1 day later)

maya: postmortem link: https://wiki.redwood/example/postmortem/7892. root cause: shard mapping change combined with high-cardinality session prefixes; mitigations: hot-prefix pinning, eviction parallelism cap, SDK guidance.

alex: closing thread.
